holidays.name: National Banana Split Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the glorious ice cream sundae made with a split banana, three scoops of ice cream, and a mountain of toppings like pineapple, strawberry, chocolate syrup, whipped cream, and a cherry on top.
holidays.origin: The banana split is credited to apprentice pharmacist David Strickler, who created it in 1904 at Tassel Pharmacy in Latrobe, Pennsylvania. The town of Latrobe celebrates its birthplace status with an annual festival.
holidays.funFact: Latrobe, Pennsylvania hosts a Great American Banana Split Festival, and the National Ice Cream Retailers Association certified the town as the birthplace of the banana split in 2013.

holidays.name: National Whiskey Sour Day
holidays.description: A toast to the classic cocktail of whiskey, lemon juice, and sugar, sometimes topped with a frothy egg white and a cherry or orange slice. Pucker up and sip responsibly.
holidays.origin: Whiskey sours date to the 19th century, with the first known recipe appearing in Jerry Thomas's 1862 bartender's guide. Sailors reportedly used citrus to fight scurvy, which helped inspire the sour style of drink.
holidays.funFact: The earliest known printed reference to a whiskey sour is from a Wisconsin newspaper in 1870, and some historians credit an Englishman who served drinks on ships.

holidays.name: Kiss and Make Up Day
holidays.description: A day to bury the hatchet, swallow your pride, and patch things up with a friend, partner, or family member. Bonus points for doing it with a kiss, a hug, or at least a sincere text message.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that grew in popularity in the 20th century as a lighthearted push toward reconciliation, with the idea that everyone has someone they should forgive or apologize to.
holidays.funFact: Studies on relationships suggest that quick apologies and affectionate gestures after arguments help couples recover faster, so this holiday is surprisingly science-backed.

holidays.name: National Park Service Founders Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the creation of the National Park Service and the great outdoors, often with free ranger events, hikes, and a general excuse to wear a flat hat.
holidays.origin: President Woodrow Wilson signed the National Park Service Organic Act on August 25, 1916, creating the agency to protect scenic landscapes, wildlife, and historic sites for future generations.
holidays.funFact: The National Park Service now manages over 400 sites, and entrance fees are often waived on its birthday, making it one of the best free days outdoors.

holidays.name: Whisk(e)y Sour Day's Rival: National Pots de Crème Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the silky, rich French custard dessert traditionally served in small pots, often flavored with chocolate, vanilla, or coffee. It is basically pudding that went to finishing school.
holidays.origin: Pots de crème originated in France, where the dessert has been served for centuries in special lidded porcelain cups called pots de crème. The modern food holiday tradition marks it in late August.
holidays.funFact: The little lidded cups designed for pots de crème are so specialized that antique sets are collector's items, and the lids were originally meant to keep the custard from forming a skin.
